title: Canary Workflow — User Stories and Edge Cases (brainstorm)
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- This is a working brainstorm to capture user stories + edge cases for Hosted canary rollout workflow as we take beta primitives to GA.
- Intentionally a little messy; we’ll pull “must-fix for GA” into PRD acceptance criteria and tickets.

Scope assumptions (for this doc)
- Deployment mode: Hosted routes only (not Dedicated/Private).
- A rollout = baseline variant + candidate variant, with weighted traffic split (percentage).
- Guardrails: error rate, latency, and token-cost delta; optional quality gate (eval/monitoring integration).
- Operators can pause / rollback quickly.
- Console is primary UX; API support exists but not deep in this doc.

Glossary (terms used below)
- Route: customer’s Hosted inference endpoint configuration.
- Baseline: current model+version configuration serving most traffic.
- Candidate: proposed model+version (or configuration) being tested.
- Sticky routing: consistent selection of variant for a user/session/request key.
- Session (streaming): a single streaming response lifecycle; retries must not mix variants.

Personas / primary users
1) Application engineer (customer)
- Wants to roll out new model version safely without downtime.
- Cares about performance, quality, and cost.

2) Platform engineer / admin (customer)
- Cares about RBAC, audit trail, guardrails, deterministic behavior across regions.

3) Redwood oncall / support
- Needs to troubleshoot “why did traffic go to candidate?”, “why is split not matching?”, “how to rollback safely?”

User stories (happy paths)
A. Create rollout
- As a user, I can create a rollout for a route by choosing:
  - baseline variant (usually the route’s current pinned model+version)
  - candidate variant (model+version, compatible with route mode/features)
  - initial traffic split (default 1–5% to candidate)
  - guardrails (recommended defaults)
  - schedule (manual steps; optional timed progression)
- UX expectation: can preview “effective routing” (what will happen per region) before saving.

B. Edit rollout
- As a user, I can change weights / schedule / guardrails, with validation and clear diff.
- UX expectation: changes show up in an activity timeline with actor + timestamp + before/after.

C. Monitor + compare
- As a user, I can view baseline vs candidate metrics side-by-side:
  - request rate, error rate (4xx/5xx), p50/p95 latency, token cost
  - plus any “quality gate” indicator (if configured)
- UX expectation: can filter by time window and region; “what changed” is visible.

D. Pause / rollback
- As a user, I can pause a rollout (stop progression, freeze traffic split) OR rollback (force 0% candidate) quickly.
- UX expectation: rollback is one click with confirmation; effective routing reflects it quickly.

E. Promote candidate (close rollout)
- As a user, I can promote candidate to become baseline and end the rollout.
- UX expectation: promotion writes a clear final state and locks history.

Edge cases + proposed product behavior

1) Route lifecycle issues
1.1 Route deleted while rollout exists
- Problem: route referenced by rollout policy no longer exists.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Control plane: mark rollout as “orphaned” (read-only) with clear error.
  - Data plane: no routing decisions needed because route no longer resolves.
  - Console: show banner “Route deleted; rollout archived”; keep audit history for retention.
- Validation: if route deletion is initiated, warn “this will end active rollout and archive history.”

1.2 Route renamed / moved to different project/org
- Proposed behavior:
  - Use immutable route_id; rename doesn’t break.
  - If route changes org/project: require policy to be reattached via admin action (avoid cross-tenant leakage).

1.3 Route config changed outside rollout
- Examples: changing max_tokens defaults, adding tools/function calling settings, changing fallback model.
- Proposed behavior:
  - If route settings are global and apply to both variants: OK.
  - If change makes baseline/candidate incompatible: block save and/or auto-pause with explanation.
  - Console should show “Route config changed since rollout started” with diff link if available.

2) Model lifecycle issues
2.1 Candidate model deprecated / removed from catalog mid-rollout
- Proposed behavior:
  - Hard stop: if candidate no longer deployable, rollout auto-pauses and candidate weight forced to 0% (safety-first).
  - Console: show “Candidate unavailable (deprecated)” with CTA to choose a new candidate.
  - Audit event should record automatic action (system actor).

2.2 Baseline model deprecated mid-rollout
- Risk: rollback may be impossible if baseline unavailable.
- Proposed behavior:
  - For Hosted we should prevent users from being in a state where rollback = broken.
  - If baseline is scheduled for deprecation, show proactive warning at rollout create time.
  - If baseline becomes unavailable: freeze at last good config, and force selection of new baseline before allowing further changes.

2.3 Version compatibility / feature parity
- Examples: candidate does not support function calling / JSON schema / max context / embeddings vs chat mismatch.
- Proposed validation:
  - At creation/edit: validate baseline/candidate both satisfy route “capabilities contract” (mode + features).
  - Console should show explicit incompatibility reasons (not generic “invalid model”).

3) Regional / availability issues
3.1 Partial region outage during rollout
- Reality: Hosted routes may have region routing; some regions may be degraded.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Effective routing preview must show per-region variant weights.
  - If a region is down and traffic fails over to another region, variant selection should still follow that region’s policy (but metrics must annotate failover to avoid “false candidate regression”).
  - Guardrails: consider whether thresholds evaluate globally or per-region.
    - Recommendation: default global evaluation for simplicity + optional per-region guardrail advanced setting (not for GA unless required).

3.2 Policy propagation lag across regions
- Known risk: user edits weights and sees inconsistent behavior.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Console: show “propagating” state with last-applied policy version per region.
  - Rollback/pause should be prioritized and fast-path where possible.

3.3 Control plane degradation
- If policy service is slow/unavailable, does data plane continue serving?
- Proposed behavior:
  - Data plane should continue with last-known-good policy.
  - Console should show staleness and last update time.

4) Traffic splitting behavior details
4.1 “Percent sum” and rounding
- Edge: weights must equal 100 but UI may allow steps like 33/67.
- Proposed validation:
  - Store integer basis points (0–10,000) or integer percent (0–100) with deterministic rounding.
  - Console shows what will actually be used (no silent rounding).

4.2 Very low traffic routes
- Edge: at 1% split, route gets 10 req/day => effectively zero candidate samples.
- Proposed UX:
  - Show warning: “Low traffic; canary may take N days to reach statistical confidence.”
  - Offer optional “minimum candidate requests per hour” suggestion (non-blocking).

4.3 Sticky routing vs pure random
- Edge: customers expect consistent experience for end users; also want fair evaluation.
- Proposed behavior (aligned w/ ADR direction):
  - Default: request-hash stickiness ON for chat/completions routes where sessions are likely.
  - Allow “random per request” advanced setting.
  - Choose stable hash keys (to be confirmed): {account_id, route_id, end_user_id? session_id?}.
  - If no stable key provided, fall back to random and show warning.

4.4 Quota / rate limiting interactions
- Edge: candidate might have higher token usage, causing org-level quota to trip, affecting baseline too.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Quota is evaluated at account/route level (existing behavior), but monitoring must break down token usage by variant.
  - Console guardrail: token-cost delta threshold should compare (candidate vs baseline) and warn that global quotas may impact both.
  - Optional future: separate per-variant quota buckets (out of GA scope).

4.5 Retries and idempotency
- Edge: clients retry 5xx/timeouts; variant selection could flip and poison comparisons.
- Proposed behavior:
  - If request has idempotency key, pin variant selection to that key for a TTL.
  - If no key: pin within a single streaming session at minimum.
  - Console / docs should recommend idempotency keys for accurate canaries.

5) Streaming + session semantics
5.1 Streaming response must not switch variants mid-stream
- Proposed behavior:
  - Selection happens at start of request and is pinned for entire stream.

5.2 Streaming failure + retry
- Edge: stream fails at token 200; client retries.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Retry should reuse original variant selection where possible.
  - If cannot reuse (missing key, selection cache expired), then:
    - prefer baseline for safety OR
    - prefer consistent hash output if deterministic keys exist.
  - Need explicit decision (lean baseline if ambiguity).

5.3 Long-lived sessions during rollout changes
- Edge: user starts a stream at 5% candidate; rollout is rolled back mid-stream.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Existing in-flight sessions complete on assigned variant.
  - Rollback affects new requests immediately (subject to propagation).
  - Console should mention “in-flight requests may continue for up to X seconds/minutes.”

6) Guardrails + safety defaults
6.1 Creating rollout without guardrails
- Proposed behavior:
  - For GA, require at least one guardrail enabled (error OR latency OR cost) unless user has elevated permission.
  - Default thresholds should be pre-populated and explained.

6.2 Setting 100% candidate immediately
- Proposed behavior:
  - Block by default (or require explicit override + admin permission + confirmation).
  - If user really wants 100%, they should use “promote” flow or set schedule steps.

6.3 Guardrail thresholds too strict -> flapping
- Edge: rollback triggers constantly due to noise.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Use minimum observation window (e.g., 5 minutes) and minimum sample size.
  - Show “insufficient data” instead of hard fail when too few requests.
  - Auto actions:
    - GA stance: start with alert-only (notify) OR allow auto-pause; auto-rollback might be too risky unless clearly configured.

6.4 Cost guardrail definition
- Edge: token cost depends on model pricing + tokens generated; variance is high.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Compare cost per successful request (or per 1k tokens) candidate vs baseline.
  - Exclude 4xx from cost delta computations by default.
  - Document method in UI tooltip.

7) Telemetry + monitoring edge cases
7.1 Metric cardinality explosion
- Edge: variant label per rollout, plus route_id and model_version can blow up.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Use fixed labels: variant={baseline|candidate} and rollout_id (optional, sampled) rather than arbitrary names.
  - Provide per-rollout dashboards via precomputed queries, not raw high-cardinality tags.

7.2 Comparing apples-to-apples
- Edge: baseline and candidate may see different user cohorts if stickiness keys change.
- Proposed behavior:
  - If stickiness enabled, ensure same keying method across baseline/candidate.
  - Console should show which stickiness mode/key is active.

7.3 “No data” states
- Proposed behavior:
  - Explicit empty state: “No candidate traffic yet” (if weight > 0 but no requests)
  - “Telemetry delayed” state (if metrics ingestion lagging)

8) RBAC / entitlements / audit logging
8.1 Who can create/edit/pause/rollback
- Proposed roles:
  - Admin: all actions
  - Developer: create/edit within guardrails; cannot override safety blocks
  - Read-only: view only
- UX expectation: UI hides disabled actions and provides permission error messaging.

8.2 Audit log contents and PII
- Edge: rollout may reference model ids, route names, schedule; could include user-provided notes.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Audit events should include before/after of policy fields, but no prompt content or end-user identifiers.
  - Console “activity timeline” should mirror audit event summaries.

9) Migration / beta users
9.1 Existing beta rollout policies
- Edge: customers already have a rollout object under beta schema.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Console detects and offers “migrate to GA rollout” with explanation.
  - Migration is deterministic; no behavior change without explicit user confirmation.
  - If migration fails validation, show detailed reasons + suggested fixes.

10) Failure modes + recommended UI states
- “Draft” vs “Active” vs “Paused” vs “Rolled back” vs “Completed” vs “Archived/Orphaned”
- We should define a small state machine that backend enforces; UI should not invent states.
- Recommended:
  - Draft (not applied)
  - Active (applied + candidate_weight > 0)
  - Paused (applied + schedule progression halted; weights remain)
  - Rolled back (applied + candidate_weight = 0)
  - Completed (candidate promoted or rollout ended)
  - Archived (route deleted / model removed)

Specific “must not happen” behaviors (regressions to avoid)
- Traffic split differs from what Console shows due to propagation, without any visible “propagating/stale” indication.
- Streaming request starts on baseline and continues on candidate (cross-variant mixing).
- User can set 100% candidate without guardrails by accident (misclick / unclear confirmation).
- Customer cannot rollback because baseline was deprecated/unavailable.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Are guardrails “alert-only” for GA or do we support auto-pause/auto-rollback on thresholds? (SRE preference likely auto-pause first.)
- Do we evaluate guardrails globally only, or allow per-region thresholds in GA?
- What is the default stickiness key and how do customers supply end_user_id / session_id safely?
- How do we represent schedule steps in the policy schema (timed vs manual) without making UI too complex?
- What is our official definition of “effective routing” when multiple layers exist (account policy + route policy + region overrides)? Need a crisp explanation.

Notes to self / follow-ups
- Add concrete examples for UI copy:
  - “Candidate weight set to 50% but only 5% of requests observed due to sticky routing and low traffic.”
  - “Rollback initiated; in-flight streams may continue for up to 60s.”
- Confirm with Security (Marcus/Kevin): audit event diff format and retention/export requirements.
- Confirm with Observability (Logan/Nadia/Thomas): exact metric dimensions and cardinality limits we will enforce for GA.
